_comment: 创伤知情教育模拟。参考幸存者中心原则与支持者指南；不评价、不量化幸存者的创伤反应或求助选择。内容待公益律师与创伤专业人员复核。

title.en: When Seeking Help Causes More Harm
title.zh: 向亲友求助后遭遇“二次伤害”怎么办

tagline.en: Practise boundaries when someone doubts, blames, pressures, exposes, or overwhelms a survivor.
tagline.zh: 当求助换来质疑、责备、逼迫、泄露或过度追问时，练习保护自己的边界。

intro.en: This scenario begins after a survivor tells someone what happened. It does not ask you to prove the experience or retell details. There is no score: freezing, leaving, delaying a decision, or changing whom you trust are all understandable responses.
intro.zh: 这个情景从幸存者向他人讲述经历之后开始，不要求你证明事情发生过，也不要求复述细节。这里没有分数：僵住、离开、暂缓决定或更换求助对象，都是可以理解的反应。

narration.en: You told someone you hoped would be safe. What response do you want to practise handling?
narration.zh: 你向一个原本以为可以信任的人讲了经历。你想练习应对哪一种反应？

coach.en: A harmful response may come from ignorance, prejudice, control, coercion, or institutional misconduct. You are not responsible for educating the person who hurt you.
coach.zh: 伤人的回应可能来自无知，也可能来自偏见、控制、胁迫或机构失当。你没有义务教育伤害你的人。

text.en: They question or blame me
text.zh: 对方质疑或责怪我

text.en: They pressure me to report — or not to report
text.zh: 对方逼我立刻报案，或逼我不要报案

text.en: They tell others or confront the person without my consent
text.zh: 对方未经同意告诉别人，或擅自去对质

text.en: A helper repeatedly demands details or asks humiliating questions
text.zh: 机构人员反复逼问细节，或提出羞辱性问题

text.en: Friends pull away because they do not know what to say
text.zh: 朋友因为不知道说什么而疏远

narration.en: They ask: “Why didn't you fight back? Why did you wait? Maybe you misunderstood.”
narration.zh: 对方问：“你为什么不反抗？为什么现在才说？是不是你误会了？”

coach.en: Freezing, appeasing, fragmented memory, and delayed disclosure are recognised trauma responses. None of them means consent, and visible injury is not a condition for being believed.
coach.zh: 僵住、顺从求生、记忆片段化和延迟披露都可能是创伤反应。它们不等于同意；是否有明显伤痕也不应成为被相信的前提。

text.en: Say: “I need you to listen, not decide whether it happened.”
text.zh: 说：“我需要你倾听，不是判断这件事有没有发生。”

feedback.en: You name what support means to you.
feedback.zh: 你明确说出了自己需要怎样的支持。

text.en: End the conversation without explaining
text.zh: 不再解释，结束这次谈话

feedback.en: You step away. A boundary does not require a debate.
feedback.zh: 你离开了。设定边界不需要先赢得一场辩论。

text.en: I freeze and cannot answer
text.zh: 我僵住了，什么也说不出来

feedback.en: Not answering is not agreement. You can decide what you need later.
feedback.zh: 没有回答不等于认同。你可以之后再决定自己需要什么。

narration.en: The conversation has left you feeling smaller and less safe.
narration.zh: 这次谈话让你感到更不安全，也更孤立。

text.en: Contact a different trusted person or professional service
text.zh: 转向另一位可信任的人或专业服务

text.en: Pause all conversations and give myself time
text.zh: 暂停谈论这件事，先给自己时间

narration.en: One person insists you report immediately. Another says reporting would “ruin the other person's future.” Both speak as if the decision belongs to them.
narration.zh: 一个人逼你立刻报案，另一个人说报案会“毁掉对方的前途”。两个人都把决定当成了自己的。

coach.en: Except where a specific mandatory-reporting duty applies, support should preserve the survivor's agency. Encouragement becomes harmful when it turns into threats, guilt, or control.
coach.zh: 除非法律对特定情形另有强制报告要求，支持应当保留幸存者的自主决定。鼓励一旦变成威胁、内疚施压或控制，就会造成新的伤害。

text.en: Say: “Give me information and options, not an ultimatum.”
text.zh: 说：“请给我信息和选项，不要替我下最后通牒。”

text.en: Ask someone neutral about medical, legal, and support options
text.zh: 向中立的专业人员了解医疗、法律和支持选项

text.en: Leave the decision for another day
text.zh: 把决定留到以后再做

narration.en: You can ask for practical help without handing over control of the decision.
narration.zh: 你可以获得实际帮助，同时不把决定权交出去。

text.en: Ask them to accompany me only if and when I choose
text.zh: 请对方只在我决定后、按我需要的方式陪同

text.en: Choose another supporter who can respect my pace
text.zh: 换一个能够尊重我节奏的支持者

narration.en: You learn that they told relatives, posted hints online, or contacted the suspected offender without asking you.
narration.zh: 你发现对方把经历告诉了亲属、在网上暗示，或未经询问就联系了涉嫌侵害者。

coach.en: A survivor's story is not community property. Unwanted disclosure can create privacy, retaliation, safety, and evidence risks.
coach.zh: 幸存者的经历不是可以随意传播的公共信息。未经同意的泄露可能带来隐私、报复、人身安全和证据风险。

text.en: State: “Do not tell or contact anyone without my permission.”
text.zh: 明确说：“未经我允许，不要告诉或联系任何人。”

text.en: Save what was shared and ask for it to be removed
text.zh: 保存泄露记录，并要求删除或停止传播

text.en: Reduce or end contact with them
text.zh: 减少或结束与对方的联系

narration.en: You consider what would help you feel safer now.
narration.zh: 你开始考虑，现在怎样做能让自己更安全。

text.en: Review account privacy and tell one trusted person what happened
text.zh: 检查账号隐私设置，并把情况告诉一位可信任的人

text.en: Ask a professional service about privacy or retaliation risks
text.zh: 向专业机构咨询隐私或报复风险

narration.en: During an interview, a helper repeats intimate questions, uses blaming language, or asks irrelevant questions about clothing and past relationships.
narration.zh: 在一次询问中，工作人员反复追问私密细节，使用责备性语言，或询问与事实无关的穿着和过往关系。

coach.en: Relevant fact-finding may still be difficult, but humiliation and repetitive irrelevant questioning are not the same as necessary clarification. You may ask why a question is relevant and what procedural support is available.
coach.zh: 必要的事实核实有时确实艰难，但羞辱和反复追问无关内容并不等于必要询问。你可以询问问题与案件有何关联，以及能获得哪些程序支持。

text.en: Ask for a pause and for the question's relevance to be explained
text.zh: 要求暂停，并请对方说明问题与案件的关联

text.en: Ask whether a lawyer, advocate, or trusted support person may attend
text.zh: 询问能否由律师、支持人员或可信任的人陪同

text.en: I cannot continue the interview right now
text.zh: 我现在无法继续这次询问

narration.en: Before continuing, you can ask about records, corrections, complaints, and available support.
narration.zh: 继续之前，你可以询问记录、更正、投诉和支持安排。

text.en: Review the written record and correct inaccurate wording before signing
text.zh: 签字前核对书面记录并更正不准确表述

text.en: Ask for a different interviewer or complaint channel
text.zh: 要求更换询问人员或了解投诉渠道

narration.en: A friend stops replying. Another changes the subject whenever you mention what happened.
narration.zh: 一位朋友不再回复，另一位每当你提起经历就立刻转移话题。

coach.en: Their discomfort does not make your needs excessive. Good support can be simple: believe, listen, ask what is needed, protect privacy, and stay patient.
coach.zh: 对方感到不知所措，不代表你的需要“太多”。有效支持可以很简单：相信、倾听、询问需要、保护隐私并保持耐心。

text.en: Ask directly whether they can listen for ten minutes
text.zh: 直接问对方能否倾听十分钟

text.en: Stop asking this person and try another support route
text.zh: 不再向这个人求助，转向其他支持渠道

text.en: Take a break from reaching out
text.zh: 暂停求助，先休息一下

narration.en: Support can come from more than one person and can change over time.
narration.zh: 支持不必只来自一个人，也可以随着时间调整。

text.en: Build a small support circle with different roles
text.zh: 建立一个分工不同的小型支持圈

text.en: Use a professional hotline or service when I am ready
text.zh: 准备好时使用专业热线或服务

title.en: You changed the source of support

summary.en: A person who doubts, blames, exposes, or controls you does not have to remain your main support. Seeking someone safer is not betrayal or failure.
summary.zh: 质疑、责备、泄露或控制你的人，不必继续成为你的主要支持者。转向更安全的人不是背叛，也不是失败。

summary.en: Pausing is a decision, too. You may return to information, support, medical care, or legal options when you are ready; a delay never transfers responsibility to you.
summary.zh: 暂停本身也是一种决定。准备好时，你仍可以重新了解支持、医疗或法律选项；延迟不会把责任转移到你身上。

summary.en: Supporters may share information and help with practical steps, but pressure and guilt are not support. Your safety, needs, and informed choice matter.
summary.zh: 支持者可以提供信息和实际帮助，但逼迫和内疚施压不是支持。你的安全、需要和知情选择都很重要。

title.en: You set a privacy and safety boundary
title.zh: 你设定了隐私与安全边界

summary.en: Unauthorised disclosure was not your fault. Preserving records, limiting contact, and asking for professional advice can help you decide what to do next.
summary.zh: 未经同意的泄露不是你的错。保存记录、限制接触并寻求专业意见，可以帮助你决定下一步。

title.zh: 你提出了程序支持需求

summary.en: You may ask about breaks, relevance, corrections, accompaniment, and complaint routes. Availability and procedure vary, but asking does not make you difficult.
summary.zh: 你可以询问暂停、问题关联性、记录更正、陪同和投诉渠道。各地程序可能不同，但提出这些要求并不代表你“难配合”。

title.en: You named the support you needed
title.zh: 你说出了自己需要的支持

detail.en: “I need you to listen, not judge” gives a willing supporter a clear role. You never owe this explanation to someone who keeps causing harm.
detail.zh: “我需要你倾听，不是评判”能让愿意支持的人知道该怎么做。面对持续伤害你的人，你没有义务反复解释。

detail.en: The survivor decides who is told, what is shared, and when, subject to any specific legal duty that may apply.
detail.zh: 原则上应由幸存者决定告诉谁、透露什么、何时透露；特定法律强制报告义务另当别论。

title.zh: 你保护了自己的决定权

detail.en: Information, accompaniment, and practical help can support a choice. Threats, guilt, and ultimatums replace it.
detail.zh: 信息、陪同和实际帮助能支持选择；威胁、内疚施压和最后通牒则会取代选择。

title.zh: 你转向了更安全的支持

detail.en: A different friend, hotline, social worker, counsellor, lawyer, or medical professional may be a better fit. You can combine forms of support.
detail.zh: 另一位朋友、热线、社工、心理人员、律师或医务人员可能更适合。不同类型的支持也可以组合使用。

detail.en: Whether accompaniment is permitted depends on the setting and procedure. Ask before the interview and request an explanation if it is refused.
detail.zh: 能否陪同取决于具体机构与程序。可在询问前提出；如被拒绝，可要求说明适用规则。

detail.en: Correct inaccurate or incomplete wording before signing, and ask what copies or receipts can be provided under the applicable procedure.
detail.zh: 签字前更正不准确或不完整的表述，并询问依适用程序可以取得哪些副本或回执。

realFlow.en: Stabilise first — pause, leave, or contact someone safer if the conversation is causing harm.
realFlow.zh: 先恢复安全感——如果谈话正在造成伤害，可以暂停、离开或联系更安全的人。

realFlow.en: Name the boundary only if useful — for example: listen without judging; do not disclose; do not contact anyone for me.
realFlow.zh: 只在对你有帮助时表达边界——例如：请倾听而不要评判；不要泄露；不要替我联系任何人。

realFlow.en: Choose support by role — emotional listening, practical accompaniment, medical care, legal information, social work, or crisis help.
realFlow.zh: 按需要选择支持——情绪倾听、实际陪同、医疗、法律信息、社工或危机援助。

realFlow.en: For an institutional interview, ask about pauses, question relevance, accompaniment, record correction, copies, and complaint channels.
realFlow.zh: 面对机构询问，可了解暂停、问题关联性、陪同、记录更正、副本和投诉渠道。

realFlow.en: If private information was disclosed, preserve the disclosure record, assess safety, request removal where appropriate, and seek professional advice if needed.
realFlow.zh: 如隐私被泄露，保存泄露记录、评估安全风险、在适当时要求删除，并按需寻求专业意见。

note.en: Additional harm caused by blaming, disbelief, forced disclosure, controlling decisions, humiliating procedures, or repeated unnecessary retelling after the original violence.
note.zh: 在原有暴力之后，由责备、不相信、强迫披露、控制决定、羞辱性程序或不必要的反复讲述造成的额外伤害。

note.en: Support that prioritises safety, trust, choice, collaboration, privacy, and avoiding re-traumatisation.
note.zh: 优先考虑安全、信任、选择、协作和隐私，并尽量避免再次触发创伤的支持方式。

note.en: Automatic survival responses. They do not mean consent and are not proof that the harm was welcomed.
note.zh: 自动发生的求生反应，不等于同意，也不能证明受害者欢迎伤害。
